The '''2008–09 Premier League''' (known as the '''[[Barclays]] Premier League''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 17th season since the establishment of the [[Premier League]] in 1992. The season began on Saturday, 16 August 2008,<ref>{{cite news |title=2008/09 fixtures announced |url=http://www.premierleague.com/page/Headlines/0,,12306~1328838,00.html |publisher=Premier League |date=16 June 2008 |access-date=16 June 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080617190824/http://www.premierleague.com/page/Headlines/0%2C%2C12306~1328838%2C00.html |archive-date=17 June 2008 |url-status=live}}</ref> and ended on 24 May 2009. The fixtures were announced on 16 June 2008. A total of 20 teams contested the league, consisting of 17 who competed in the previous season and three promoted from the [[Football League Championship]]. The new match ball was the [[Nike Inc.|Nike]] T90 Omni.

[[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] began the season as the two-time defending champions, having secured their second consecutive (and tenth) Premier League title on the final day of the [[2007–08 Premier League|previous season]].

==Season summary==
At the start of the season, clubs were allowed to name seven substitutes on the bench instead of five.<ref>{{cite news |title=Premier League ratifies more subs |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/7233663.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=7 February 2008 |access-date=7 June 2008 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080210214914/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7233663.stm |archive-date=10 February 2008}}</ref> This season was also different in that there was no New Year's Day game, as is traditional. This was because the FA Cup third round is traditionally played on the first Saturday in January, which in 2009 fell in the usual spot for New Year's league games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-league.co.uk/page/FLExplainedDetail/0,,10794~1356571,00.html |title=How the fixture list is compiled |access-date=17 December 2008 |date=16 June 2008 |publisher=The Football League |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140413193841/http://www.football-league.co.uk/page/FLExplainedDetail/0%2C%2C10794~1356571%2C00.html |archive-date=13 April 2014 |url-status=dead}}</ref> September saw [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] taken over by the [[Abu Dhabi United Group]], transforming the football club into one of the world's wealthiest, securing the signing of [[Robinho]] for a British record £32.5&nbsp;million just seconds before the 2008 summer transfer window closed in the process.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arab group agrees Man City deal |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/m/man_city/7591735.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=1 September 2008 |access-date=1 September 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080902041338/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/m/man_city/7591735.stm |archive-date=2 September 2008 |url-status=live}}</ref>

The first goal of the season was scored by [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]'s [[Samir Nasri]] against newly promoted [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] in the fourth minute of the early kick-off game on the opening day of the season on 16 August.<ref name="first_goal">{{cite news |first=Paul |last=Fletcher |title=Arsenal 1–0 West Brom |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7551128.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=16 August 2008 |access-date=16 August 2008}}</ref> [[Gabriel Agbonlahor]] of [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] scored the first [[hat-trick]] of the season against Manchester City, scoring three goals in the space of seven minutes.<ref name="villamancity">{{cite news |first=Chris |last=Bevan |title=Aston Villa 4–2 Man City |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/7551172.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=17 August 2008 |access-date=17 August 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080829003203/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7551172.stm |archive-date=29 August 2008 |url-status=live}}</ref>

The title race was a battle between Manchester United and bitter rivals [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], who beat them 4–1 at [[Old Trafford]] on 14 March 2009. Liverpool topped the table at the end of 2008, but their lead slipped after a series of draws. On 16 May 2009, Manchester United clinched the Premier League title after a goalless draw against Arsenal. It was their 11th Premier League title and 18th English top flight title overall, tying a record with Liverpool, who finished as runners-up. It was the second time that they had won the title for three consecutive years, the first being in 2001. Only four other clubs have achieved this feat: [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]] (1923–25), Arsenal (1933–35), Liverpool (1982–84) and Manchester City (2021–24), with the latter becoming the first club to win the English top flight title for four consecutive seasons.

[[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] were the first team to be relegated to the [[Football League Championship|Championship]] after losing 2–0 at home to Liverpool on 17 May 2009. [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] and [[Newcastle United]] joined them on the last day of the season after losses at [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] and Aston Villa, respectively. The results meant that [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] and [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] stayed up, despite home defeats to Manchester United and Chelsea respectively. The fact that Hull City avoided relegation (along with [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]], who stayed up relatively comfortably under the management of [[Tony Pulis]]), meant it was the first time since the [[2005–06 FA Premier League|2005–06 season]] that more than one promoted club maintained their Premier League status. Aston Villa, [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] and [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]], who stayed up last season on goal difference, all secured European football for the 2009–10 season through their league positions.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ups and downs |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/7969096.stm |publisher=BBC Sport |date=24 May 2009 |access-date=25 May 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090602045109/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/7969096.stm |archive-date=2 June 2009 |url-status=live}}</ref>

==Teams==
Twenty teams competed in the league&nbsp;– the top seventeen teams from the previous season and the three teams promoted from the [[2007–08 Football League Championship|Championship]]. The promoted teams were [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]], [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] (returning to the top flight after absences of two and twenty-three years respectively) and [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] (playing top flight football for the first time ever). This was also Stoke City's first season in the Premier League. They replaced [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] (relegated to the [[2008–09 Football League Championship|Championship]] after a two-year top-flight spell), [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] and [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] (both teams relegated to the Championship after a season's presence).

# {{note|1}} West Ham United's shirt sponsor was [[XL Leisure Group|XL Holidays]] until 12 September 2008 after the company was placed into administration.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/w/west_ham_utd/7611752.stm |title=West Ham end shirt sponsor deal |publisher=BBC Sport |date=12 September 2008 |access-date=24 February 2026}}</ref> The club ran sponsorless until 3 December 2008 when the deal with SBOBET was announced.

Also, [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]] provided new match balls, white with red and yellow (autumn/spring) and yellow with purple and black (winter), based on their T90 Laser II Omni model.

* {{note|1|1}} Newcastle United manager Joe Kinnear was originally appointed as interim manager until the end of October on 26 September, signed a one-month contract extension on 24 October, and was named manager until the end of the English football season on 28 November.
* {{note|2|2}} Portsmouth caretaker manager Paul Hart was appointed on 9 February. On 3 March chairman [[Alexandre Gaydamak]] confirmed the appointment would be until at least the end of the English football season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Hart to stay at Pompey for season |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/p/portsmouth/7922491.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=3 March 2009 |access-date=20 March 2009 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090306181417/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/p/portsmouth/7922491.stm| archive-date= 6 March 2009 | url-status= live}}</ref>
* {{note|3|3}} Chelsea manager Guus Hiddink remained [[Russia national football team|Russia]] manager until the end of the English football season, when he left Chelsea and returned to his Russia duties on a full-time basis.
* {{note|4|4}} Newcastle United manager Joe Kinnear took leave from Newcastle United following heart bypass surgery on 16 February. His assistants, [[Chris Hughton]] and [[Colin Calderwood]], were appointed to serve as caretaker managers until his return, which was understood might not occur before the end of the English football season. On 31 March, Alan Shearer was appointed manager until the end of the season, as Joe Kinnear was not able to return to his Newcastle United duties until the end of the English football season. After the season ended, both Joe Kinnear and Alan Shearer left the club permanently, and Chris Hughton was appointed manager during the course of the following season.
* {{note|5|5}} Roberto Martínez was announced to be manager on 9 June, however due to complications surrounding the appointment of backroom staff, the deal was not finalised and officially announced until 15 June.

==Season statistics==

===Scoring===
* First goal of the season: [[Samir Nasri]] for Arsenal against West Bromwich, 3&nbsp;minutes and 40&nbsp;seconds. (<small>''16 August 2008''</small>).<ref name="first_goal" />
* Last goal of the season: [[Kenwyne Jones]] for Sunderland against Chelsea, 90&nbsp;minutes. (<small>''24 May 2009''</small>)
* Fastest goal in a match: '''31 seconds''' – [[Steve Sidwell]] for Aston Villa against Everton (<small>''7 December 2008''</small>))<ref>{{cite news |first=Ian |last=Hughes |title=Everton 2–3 Aston Villa |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/7752881.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=7 December 2008 |access-date=16 December 2008 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20081211112200/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7752881.stm| archive-date= 11 December 2008 | url-status= live}}</ref>
* Goal scored at the latest point in a match: '''90+4&nbsp;minutes and 56 seconds''' – [[Carlton Cole]] for West Ham United against Blackburn (<small>''30 August 2008''</small>)<ref>{{cite news |title=West Ham vs Blackburn |url=http://www.espnstar.com/football/premier-league/results/report/matchplay/item92683/?matchId=3003080 |publisher=ESPN Star Sports |date=19 October 2008 |access-date=18 February 2009|url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120225040615/http://www.espnstar.com/football/premier-league/results/report/matchplay/item92683/?matchId=3003080 |archive-date=25 February 2012 }}</ref>
* First own goal of the season: [[Robert Huth]] (Middlesbrough) for Tottenham Hotspur, 90+2&nbsp;minutes and 28&nbsp;seconds (<small>''16 August 2008''</small>)<ref>{{cite news |title=Middlesbrough vs Tottenham |url=http://www.espnstar.com/football/premier-league/fixtures/matchplay/item94368/?matchId=3002944 |publisher=ESPN Star Sports |date=16 August 2008 |access-date=15 February 2009|url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120225042237/http://www.espnstar.com/football/premier-league/fixtures/matchplay/item94368/?matchId=3002944 |archive-date=25 February 2012 }}</ref>
* First hat-trick of the season and fastest hat-trick of the season: [[Gabriel Agbonlahor]] (Aston Villa) against Manchester City, 7&nbsp;minutes and 3&nbsp;seconds (<small>''17 August 2008''</small>)<ref name="villamancity" />
* Most goals scored by one player in a match: '''4 goals''' – [[Andrey Arshavin]] (Arsenal) against Liverpool, 36', 67', 70', 90' (<small>''21 April 2009''</small>)<ref name="liver4arsen4">{{cite news |first=Caroline |last=Cheese |title=Liverpool 4–4 Arsenal |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/8010701.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=21 April 2009 |access-date=21 April 2009 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090424061703/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/8010701.stm| archive-date= 24 April 2009 | url-status= live}}</ref>
* Widest winning margin: '''6 goals''' – Manchester City 6–0 Portsmouth (<small>''21 September 2008''</small>)<ref>{{cite news |first=Chris |last=Whyatt |title=Man City 6–0 Portsmouth |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/7613925.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=21 September 2008 |access-date=17 December 2008 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080925093320/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7613925.stm| archive-date=25 September 2008| url-status= live}}</ref>
* Most goals in a match: '''8 goals'''
** Arsenal 4–4 Tottenham Hotspur (<small>''29 October 2008''</small>)<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Arsenal 4–4 Tottenham |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7684610.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=29 October 2008 |access-date=2 November 2008 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20081102001458/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7684610.stm| archive-date= 2 November 2008 | url-status= live}}</ref>
** Liverpool 4–4 Arsenal (<small>''21 April 2009''</small>)<ref name="liver4arsen4" />
* Most goals in one half: '''7 goals''' – Liverpool v Arsenal (<small>''21 April 2009''</small>) 0–1 at half time, 4–4 final<ref name="liver4arsen4" />
* Most goals in one half by a single team: '''5 goals''' – Manchester United v Tottenham Hotspur (<small>''25 April 2009''</small>) 0–2 at half-time, 5–2 final<ref>{{cite news |first=Gemma |last=Thompson |title=United 5 Spurs 2 |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/Fixtures-And-Results/Match-Reports/2009/Apr/United-5-Spurs-2.aspx |work=manutd.com |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=25 April 2009 |access-date=11 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131115073252/http://www.manutd.com/en/Fixtures-And-Results/Match-Reports/2009/Apr/United-5-Spurs-2.aspx |archive-date=15 November 2013 }}</ref>

===Clean sheets===
* Most clean sheets – Manchester United (24)
* Fewest clean sheets – Hull City (6)

===Discipline===
* First yellow card of the season: [[Sam Ricketts]] for Hull City against Fulham, 28&nbsp;minutes and 6&nbsp;seconds (<small>''16 August 2008''</small>)<ref>{{cite news |title=Hull Roar To Win Over Fulham |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/8/main/2008/08/16/821614/hull-roar-to-win-over-fulham |publisher=goal.com |date=16 August 2008 |access-date=11 December 2013 }}</ref>
* First red card of the season: [[Mark Noble]] for West Ham United against Manchester City, 37&nbsp;minutes and 20&nbsp;seconds (<small>''24 August 2008''</small>)<ref>{{cite news |title=City crush 10-man Hammers |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/2475/report |publisher=Sky Sports |date=16 August 2008 |access-date=11 December 2013 }}{{dead link|date=November 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>
* Card given at latest point in a game: [[Michael Dawson (footballer)|Michael Dawson]] (red) at '''90+8&nbsp;minutes and 28 seconds''' for Tottenham Hotspur against Stoke City (<small>''19 October 2008''</small>)<ref>{{cite news |title=Stoke vs Tottenham |url=http://www.espnstar.com/football/premier-league/results/report/matchplay/item127665/?matchId=3023049 |publisher=ESPN Star Sports |date=19 October 2008 |access-date=15 February 2009|url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120225051208/http://www.espnstar.com/football/premier-league/results/report/matchplay/item127665/?matchId=3023049 |archive-date=25 February 2012 }}</ref>
* Most yellow cards in a single match: '''8'''
** Chelsea 1–1 Manchester United – one for Chelsea ([[Mikel John Obi]]) and seven for Manchester United ([[Paul Scholes]], [[Rio Ferdinand]], [[Gary Neville]], [[Dimitar Berbatov]], [[Wayne Rooney]], [[Patrice Evra]] and [[Cristiano Ronaldo]]) (<small>''21 September 2008''</small>)<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Chelsea 1–1 Man Utd |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/7613923.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=21 September 2008 |access-date=18 November 2008 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080923234352/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7613923.stm |archive-date=23 September 2008 }}</ref>
** Sunderland 1–1 Arsenal – three for Sunderland ([[Dean Whitehead]], [[Kieran Richardson]] and [[Dwight Yorke]]) and five for Arsenal ([[Gaël Clichy]], [[Kolo Touré]], [[Alex Song]], [[Nicklas Bendtner]] and [[Emmanuel Adebayor]]) (<small>''4 October 2008''</small>)<ref>{{cite news |first=Ian |last=Hughes |title=Sunderland 1–1 Arsenal |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/7639462.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=4 October 2008 |access-date=4 October 2008 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20081007104238/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7639462.stm| archive-date=7 October 2008| url-status= live}}</ref>
** Aston Villa 2–2 Arsenal – four for Aston Villa ([[Gabriel Agbonlahor]], [[Nigel Reo-Coker]], [[Stiliyan Petrov]] and [[Gareth Barry]]) and four for Arsenal ([[Alex Song]], [[Kolo Touré]], [[Abou Diaby]] and [[Robin van Persie]]) (<small>''26 December 2008''</small>)<ref>{{cite news |first=Ian |last=Hughes |title=Aston Villa 2–2 Arsenal |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/7787537.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=26 December 2008 |access-date=11 January 2009 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090111022237/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7787537.stm| archive-date= 11 January 2009 | url-status= live}}</ref>
** Manchester United 3–0 Chelsea – three for Manchester United ([[Cristiano Ronaldo]], [[Wayne Rooney]] and [[Park Ji-sung]]) and five for Chelsea ([[Frank Lampard]], [[José Bosingwa]], [[Ricardo Carvalho]], [[John Terry]] and [[Juliano Belletti]]) (<small>''11 January 2009''</small>)<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Man Utd 3–0 Chelsea |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/7808369.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=11 January 2009 |access-date=11 January 2009 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090116123254/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7808369.stm| archive-date= 16 January 2009 | url-status= live}}</ref>
** Manchester City 1–0 Sunderland – three for Manchester City ([[Valeri Bojinov]], [[Gélson Fernandes]] and [[Shaun Wright-Phillips]]) and five for Sunderland ([[Phil Bardsley]], [[Calum Davenport]], [[Grant Leadbitter]], [[Andy Reid (Irish footballer)|Andy Reid]] and [[Anton Ferdinand]]) (<small>''22 March 2009''</small>)<ref>{{cite news |first=Saj |last=Chowdhury |title=Man City 1–0 Sunderland |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/7937109.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=22 March 2009 |access-date=21 May 2009 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090327100850/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7937109.stm |archive-date=27 March 2009 }}</ref>
* Most red cards in a single match: '''3''' – Manchester City 1–2 Tottenham Hotspur – two for Manchester City ([[Richard Dunne]] and [[Gélson Fernandes]]) and one for Tottenham Hotspur ([[Benoît Assou-Ekotto]]) (<small>''9 November 2008''</small>)<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=Dawkes |title=Man City 1–2 Tottenham |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7709050.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=9 November 2008 |access-date=9 November 2008 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20081109153620/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7709050.stm| archive-date=9 November 2008| url-status= live}}</ref>

* Most goals conceded – West Bromwich Albion (67)
